reason: This passage from Ezra (likely Ezra 3) describes the rebuilding of the Second Temple after the Babylonian exile. The text focuses on the leaders (Joshua, Zerubbabel, and the priests) actively working with and mobilizing the people to rebuild the altar, offer sacrifices, and celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles. The only emotional expression involving leaders is weeping (בְּעֵינֵיהֶם בֹּכִים בְּקוֹל גָּדוֹל) by older priests and Levites at the temple's foundation, which appears to be nostalgic remembrance of the first temple rather than complaints about the people. The passage emphasizes collective action and celebration, with the people shouting praise (הָעָם הֵרִיעוּ תְרוּעָה גְדוֹלָה), not leaders expressing grievances about them.
